story: At 3:17 on a mild Thursday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is stepping onto pickleball court one at the Rec Center, where Donna is coaching him to keep his paddle up and tap the ball softly over the net. Across the street-side paths, Hal is walking the Magnolia Loop with his log, counting the pink flamingos in Donna's flock. Back at home, Rosa is sitting in her kitchen, checking off finished items on her list and jotting down anything she still needs from the store.
events: Gary (pickleball court 1): Grab a paddle and step onto court one to warm up with Donna
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and write the number in my log
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Review my list, cross off finished items, and note any last-minute shopping

gary.thought_process: Donna's waiting at court one and already told me the kitchen rule is coming while we warm up. I said my piece last tick about being slaughtered, so no need to repeat it. The cart parade stuff is stuck waiting on Hal's written approval, so nothing to do about that right now. Best move is to join her at the court, get a feel for the kitchen rule, and keep her company. Staying useful and having a neighbor who cares is what matters, and the ladder standings can wait until after we've warmed up.

parameters.content: Grab a paddle and step onto court one to warm up with Donna

donna.thought_process: Gary's here, stretched and ready, and I already told him to grab a paddle and meet me at court one. No more recruiting talk needed, time to actually teach. Start with the kitchen rule and a few easy dinks, keep it encouraging so he sticks with me as my doubles partner for the ladder. Also the Tuesday reservation is two hours, within the L-05 limit, so I'm covered.

parameters.content: Perfect, Gary, nobody's slaughtering anybody today. Stand right behind that line, keep the paddle out front, and just tap it softly over the net to me. Soft hands win this game, not strong knees.

hal.thought_process: Nobody's around, and I'm standing on Magnolia Loop with Donna's flamingo flock right in front of me. My last memory is that I'd planned to count the street-visible flamingos and log the number. L-02 caps it at three, and I want the count to hold up under review. Gary's cart paperwork can wait until I see his measurements. Count first, then report with facts, not guesses.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and write the number in my log

rosa.thought_process: Dinner prep is basically done. I've tasted the beans, set out plates, counted seats, and confirmed Friday evening is clear on my shift schedule. Nobody is around to talk to, and I've already repeated most of these checks several times this morning. One loose end is worth tying up: a small cushion of time to make sure nothing is left on my list. Rather than re-tasting the food a fifth time, I'll go over the list one last time, cross off what's done, and note anything I still need to fetch, like extra chairs or napkins, so I can stop fussing and just enjoy the evening.

parameters.content: Review my list, cross off finished items, and note any last-minute shopping

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
